name: Ascendant Semantics
description: Defines orientation, approach, self-positioning, response framing, entry, presentation, and threshold domains.

coreDomains.name: Orientation
coreDomains.definition: The reference direction from which experience is initially approached.
boundaries: Orientation is not total identity.
Orientation may change in expression across contexts.
Requires sign, ruler, or aspect information for specification.

coreDomains.name: Initial Approach
coreDomains.definition: The manner in which contact with a situation, environment, or person begins.
boundaries: Initial approach is not the entire interaction.
Does not prove conscious intention.
May be revised after contact begins.

coreDomains.name: Self-Positioning
coreDomains.definition: The way the self is situated relative to an environment, threshold, or counterpart.
boundaries: Does not imply dominance or submission.
May be embodied, psychological, or situational.
Requires a reference environment or counterpart.

coreDomains.name: Response Framing
coreDomains.definition: The initial structure that makes some cues, options, or responses more salient than others.
boundaries: Does not determine the final response.
Does not replace Mercury's interpretation.
Must not become a fixed personality claim.

coreDomains.name: Entry
coreDomains.definition: The transition from nonparticipation into active contact with a context.
boundaries: Entry is a threshold process.
Does not guarantee continued participation.
Must remain distinct from house context.

coreDomains.name: Embodied Presentation
coreDomains.definition: The observable posture, pacing, manner, or presence through which orientation becomes visible.
boundaries: Does not determine physical appearance.
Does not prove internal identity.
May vary with context and development.

coreDomains.name: Selective Attention
coreDomains.definition: The initial prioritization of cues according to the active reference frame.
boundaries: Filtering is not the whole Ascendant function.
Does not prove conscious selection.
Must remain distinct from Mercury's analysis.

coreDomains.name: Interaction Threshold
coreDomains.definition: The boundary condition at which self and environment begin to affect one another.
boundaries: The threshold is not a house.
It requires both self-side and environment-side reference.
It may be activated by timing without becoming an event guarantee.

domainRelationships.relationship: Approach becomes entry when contact begins.
The reference frame organizes initial salience and response options.
Positioning becomes visible through posture, pacing, and presence.
The Ascendant threshold remains paired with the Descendant relational reference frame.

semanticExclusions: Do not derive total personality from orientation.
Do not derive physical appearance from embodied presentation.
Do not derive false self from masking.
Do not derive conscious intent from initial approach.
Do not derive planetary action from the Ascendant.
Do not derive complete identity from first contact.

provenance.sourcePolicy: Reference-frame vocabulary only. The Ascendant may orient other functions but may not become a planet, sign, house, personality label, or finished reading.
